newsitem.title: USA: AT&T sues California Internet access provider.
newsitem.headline: AT&T sues California Internet access provider.

text.p: AT&T Corp said Tuesday it had filed suit against a California-based Internet access provider, Connect America, and its affiliates, alleging that the group defrauded AT&T of millions of dollars.
AT&T said the $7 million suit alleges that the group set up fictitious accounts on AT&T's toll-free service and resold the service to Internet service providers.
"They weren't paying AT&T, and their customers were paying them for the service they were defrauding AT&T of," said AT&T spokeswoman Janet Wyles.
The suit, filed July 28 in U.S. District Court for the Central District of California, also names Connect America's parent company, ICB Telecommunications, and OneSource Communications.
Calls to Connect America's offices in Riverside, Calif., were not answered. ICB and OneSource could not be reached for comment.
AT&T said the suit alleges the group is guilty of wire-fraud racketeering, civil conspiracy and violations of the Communications Act.
AT&T said it is seeking an injunction and an attachment of the defendants' assets, and compensatory and punitive damages.
AT&T said it might name other defendants as the suit progresses.
